name: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2, NeT-SewerOverflow), MT rows
operator: US EPA (ECHO); reports filed by permittees through NeT-SewerOverflow
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water free text in a child table (often blank)
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO; table sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv joined to sewer_overflow_bypass_receiving_waters.csv on sewer_overflow_bypass_event_key; filter permit_identifier prefix. Pipeline already has pipeline/ingest/echo_sewer_overflow_events.py. Trimmed sample in raw/sobe-sample.json.
cadence: Extract rebuilt daily; these are the 5-day written reports, so they appear days to weeks after the event (start-to-receipt median n/a).
history: Rows from April 2023 (NeT pilot) to date
license: EPA public data; no restriction stated
legal_basis: 40 CFR 127 (NPDES eRule Phase 2, from 2025-12-21); 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) five-day written report
status_reason: 0 MT event(s) in the 2026-11-03 extract; the state's permittees do not file through NeT. Montana permittees report on DEQ's own SSO form.

name: Montana DEQ Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO) Event Form (Rev. 2.0, April 2020)
status_reason: Written 5-day report under ARM 17.30.1342(12)(f)(i) after a 24-hour oral report. Asks for start/end time, volume and method, lat/long, receiving water, manhole number, whether the SSO reached water. Reports go to DEQ only; no public output found.
notes: If DEQ ever publishes these, they carry every field the event model needs.

name: MPDES municipal permit standard conditions (e.g. MT0020168): 24-hour notice of noncompliance
status_reason: Report 'as soon as possible, but no later than twenty-four (24) hours' to the Water Protection Bureau or DES; written within five days. No public notification clause found in this permit; Missoula's permit (MT0022594) is a scanned image and could not be searched.

name: Montana DEQ spill/complaint reporting and enforcement spill policy
operator: Montana DEQ Enforcement Program; DES Duty Officer
status_reason: Spill policy (rev. 2025-10-24): releases reported to the DES 24-hour line (406) 431-0411; spills that 'enter or may enter state water' must go to the NRC. Covers petroleum and hazardous substances; sewage not named. No public spill list found.

name: Montana HAB reports and advisories map (HAB.mt.gov, DPHHS and DEQ)
status_reason: HAB.mt.gov redirects to DPHHS's HAB page with a public map of reported blooms and health advisories (2026: Lake Helena, Canyon Ferry, Cooney Reservoir in June). The feature service behind the map was not traced (Public_Harmful_Algal_Bloom_Reports_WFL1 holds only base layers).

name: Montana DEQ Harmful Algal Bloom Observations Story Map
status_reason: Narrative; no service URL in its data.

name: Montana news coverage of wastewater discharges (Warm Springs Creek 2023, Columbia Falls, Holland Lake)
status_reason: The only public trace of most discharges; DEQ press releases cover enforcement.
